flawed_step: Step 3: the claim that the degree sequence decides which vertex degrees are adjacent to which, and so fixes the tree up to isomorphism, is not justified. The degree sequence records only how many vertices have each degree, not which vertices are joined.
counterexample: Both trees have degree sequence (3,2,2,1,1,1). T1: edges c-a, a-l1, c-b, b-l2, c-x (a "spider" with legs of length 2, 2 and 1). T2: edges c-a, a-b, b-l1, c-x, c-y (legs of length 3, 1 and 1). In T1 the degree-3 vertex is adjacent to two degree-2 vertices. In T2 it is adjacent to only one. So the trees are not isomorphic.
assessment_summary:
Proof attempt (induction on n, the number of vertices), with each step judged:
1. Base cases n ≤ 3: each degree sequence belongs to only one tree (K1, K2, P3). JUSTIFIED: you can check this directly.
2. Inductive step: take trees T and T' with the same degree sequence and n ≥ 4 vertices. Each has a leaf, since a tree has at least two leaves. Remove a leaf v from T and a leaf v' from T'. JUSTIFIED: removing a leaf leaves a tree.
3. Choose the leaves so that their neighbours have the same degree. Then T−v and T'−v' have the same degree sequence, and by induction they are isomorphic. Claim: the isomorphism can be extended by mapping v to v'. NOT JUSTIFIED. An isomorphism φ from T−v to T'−v' need not send v's neighbour u to v''s neighbour u'. The degree sequence does not say which vertices are adjacent, so there may be no isomorphism that sends u to u'. Also, the neighbours of all available leaves may have different degrees in T and T'.
4. So T is isomorphic to T', which finishes the induction. NOT JUSTIFIED: this depends on step 3.
5. The statement follows for all n. NOT JUSTIFIED: this depends on steps 3 and 4.

Step 3 cannot be repaired, because the statement is false. T1 has edges c-a, a-l1, c-b, b-l2, c-x. T2 has edges c-a, a-b, b-l1, c-x, c-y. Both are trees (6 vertices, 5 edges, connected), and both have degree sequence (3,2,2,1,1,1). An isomorphism preserves both degrees and adjacency. In T1 the single degree-3 vertex has two degree-2 neighbours; in T2 it has only one. Therefore no isomorphism exists, and the statement is false.
